quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: What else was on full display was Al Horford not being in Boston. Al Horford not being in Boston, Al has guarded Joel great anytime that they faced up in the regular season and playoffs. And it's a large part of their dominance over the Sixers up until this point. You get in there now, you're starting Luke Garza in Game 7 of the NBA playoffs. I didn't quite have that on my bingo cards. Ron Harper Jr., who's turned out to be a solid player, starting. Bailey Sharman, who's a rookie, who didn't start a ton of games this year, also starts. And turn the team that lives and died by the three, shot 27% from the three and all three of those guys combined for zero points. Now, I was a bit surprised by this starting lineup because I think it's a Game 7, I think you got to go all out and so for me, my starters would have been Payton Pritchard, Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Neemias Queta, and Sam Hauser.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green criticizes the Celtics' coaching staff for their unexpected Game 7 starting lineup, questioning the decision to bench Al Horford and start inexperienced players, which he believes contributed to their loss.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: I found something very interesting that Tyrese Maxey said that most people don't understand. He said, 'Once we found out JT was out, we felt like the game was going to be even harder.' And I know what he means by that. Number one, you prepare for six games to face Jayson Tatum. And now you're going into this one-game series, which is Game 7, with not a real understanding of who they're going to start, what they're going to do, what type of offense are they going to run now, what will be their scheme to try to make up for Jayson Tatum not being out there. And so what Tyrese Maxey is saying is like, 'We thought the game would be harder,' because, 'Hey, we just haven't faced this particular team that we're about to face now. We haven't faced for six games in a row. We've been preparing this team now for six games in a row, and now all of a sudden that whole thing changes because Jayson Tatum is not out there.' And I thought that was an an interesting statement, but a very mature statement by Tyrese Maxey.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Tyrese Maxey's mature insight, explaining how Jayson Tatum's unexpected absence in Game 7 made preparation harder for the opposing team, highlighting the strategic challenges of last-minute lineup changes.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: I know a lot of people are saying like, 'Yo, is this a legacy game for Joel Embiid?' And I say no, hell no. Joel Embiid is a great player. Joel Embiid is an NBA MVP. Joel Embiid is all of those things: gold medalist, perennial All-Star, one of the best bigs in this league. Joel Embiid also for those same reasons is the reason that a game in the first round, I don't care if it's Game 7 or Game 2 or 7, doesn't matter, because it's still a first-round game. In order for Joel Embiid to have legacy games, Joel Embiid has to get to the Conference Finals. And then Joel Embiid needs to help push that team to the NBA Finals. I don't think if you spoke to Joel Embiid, he would say, 'Oh man, that game I had in Round 1 this year versus Boston is a legacy game.' Now you feel good about it, you feel great about it, you're moving on, right? All of those things. Like, yeah, you feel great about it, but the job's not done.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green firmly states that Joel Embiid's Game 7 performance, while impressive, is not a 'legacy game' because true legacy-defining moments occur in the Conference Finals or NBA Finals, not the first round.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Joel, can he stay healthy will be the ultimate question. It seems like every game he's out there, he fall, he grabs something and you're just like holding your breath, you're tense, right? Like, 'Not again.' And so, what we ultimately need to see is Joel stay healthy. And if Joel can stay healthy, then what does this Philly team turn out to be? But they will turn out to be nothing if Joel doesn't stay healthy. So I think that's what to watch for. We all know how talented Joel is, but ultimately, as these games get tougher, as the pace picks up more, as it gets more physical, will Joel's body end up being able to withstand the test that is the NBA playoffs on a run to a possible NBA Finals? Will his body ultimately be able to hold up? I'm crossing my fingers, I hope so, but that is the question.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green identifies Joel Embiid's health as the paramount factor for the 76ers' playoff success, questioning whether his body can endure the increased physicality and demands of deeper playoff rounds.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown went on his stream yesterday and called out Joel Embiid, said 'Flopping has ruined our league. Joel Embiid is one of the greatest players that has played basketball, but he flops and he knows it too.' And I thought that was interesting because Joel definitely will embellish some calls a bit, you know, and Joel will play the get-foul game a bit. And ultimately, I think earlier in Joel's career, it's some of the reason why he struggled during the playoffs and his team struggled because normally, they don't call any of that stuff in the playoffs. I've been watching the playoffs this year pretty intensely, and I will say more things, and it's a game-to-game thing, right? Like you watch that Toronto game yesterday... and there wasn't much calls at all. You watch some of these other games and there's ticky-tack fouls called. So, I'm accustomed to the playoffs where you don't get much call at all, and if you're embellishing a foul, you're trying to get a call, they usually don't call it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green acknowledges Joel Embiid's tendency to flop and how it historically affects his playoff performance, while also subtly criticizing Jaylen Brown for making such comments after a loss.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Big question is what's next for this Boston team? Is it the end of the Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum era? And I would say no. I don't think it's the end of their era because look at the success they had this year with Jayson Tatum out most of the year, and then Jayson Tatum coming back and them having success. Ultimately getting ahead to a 3-1 lead. Obviously they squandered the lead away, but you got right where you want to be. Jayson Tatum unfortunately not able to play in Game 7, and I think that's more of a bigger concern than them squandering away a 3-1 lead. You know, shit happens, give Philly credit, they played well. But Jayson Tatum's knee, out of nowhere, it's hurting. Can't go in Game 7. Surprise. This is a guy who plays all the games by the way. Obviously missed games this year due to the Achilles, but Jayson Tatum plays and he plays through things. And so for him to sit out Game 7 was really worrisome to me because I'm like, 'Man, it must be something more.'
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green expresses concern about Jayson Tatum's knee injury, suggesting it's a bigger issue than the Celtics' 3-1 collapse, and questions the team's future roster construction around Tatum and Jaylen Brown.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Isaiah Stewart was a dominant force in that series. Defensively, protecting the rim, bringing a level of physicality that you got to bring to the game when you're down 3-1 if you're going to have a chance to come back. I tip my hat to Isaiah Stewart. Just getting it done by any means necessary, being that force. You see the young fella struggling. So a good young fella, I got you. Watch this. Tip my hat to Isaiah Stewart. He was the X, obviously Tobias did what Tobias needed to do, but the X-factor in that series for the Pistons was Isaiah Stewart. So I tip my cap to him.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green identifies Isaiah Stewart as the 'X-factor' for the Pistons' 3-1 comeback, praising his defensive physicality and ability to step up when a teammate like Jalen Duren struggled.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Jarrett Allen finally stepped up and had a huge game with 22 points, 19 rebounds, and three blocks. I guess he got over his fear of the lights being too bright. Start yelling at RJ Barrett in the final seconds, 'Go home! Go home!' Like, I love to see guys on that type of time. And when you step up and have a game like that, Jarrett Allen, you can talk like that. You can show up like that. Problem is, Jarrett Allen, we've seen you can do it. We've seen the lights dim for you a bit. Can you keep that going in the second round? Because guess what, them lights get brighter and brighter as teams drop off. It's less teams now, it is eight teams left in the NBA playoffs, not 16. Can you do that again? Right? So I think that's that's one of the keys for the Cavs. Can you get, you know, when James first got traded to the Cavaliers, it unlocked Jarrett Allen. And then it kind of went back down again. Saw James say yesterday when he's playing with that type of force, we're a completely different team. And it's true. They're going to need him or Evan Mobley to play at that level. Now, in an ideal world, you get both of those guys playing at that level. That hasn't quite been the case with this ball club, getting those two both of those guys playing at an extremely high level together.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Jarrett Allen's dominant Game 7 performance but challenges him to maintain that level of play and confidence as the playoff intensity increases, highlighting his past struggles with consistency.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Now we will move into these Conference Semifinals matchups and that is the 76ers versus the Knicks. They split the season series 2-2. Knicks come in rested with their last game being Thursday. Ultimately, you always wonder, is it rest versus rust? And quite honestly, they played Thursday, playing again on Monday, that's not enough time to get rusty. It is enough time to get rested. And so I think that ultimately bodes well for the New York Knicks. Now, coming into this in this series, you got to look at what matchups are going to be key in this series. Obviously, you got Embiid versus KAT. They'll have to guard each other, unless you do something funky with the matchups. But more than likely, they're going to have to guard each other. KAT is a tough matchup for Embiid because he's going to pull him out away from the rim. You got to be up on that trail three. So with that being said, I'm not sure I'm putting Embiid on KAT. You may have to throw Paul George on him to start the game. Because him pulling Embiid out, like you need Embiid healthy to have a chance to win this series. And him pulling Embiid out away from the basket, it just creates more torque on the body, creates more movement on his knees, puts him in a vulnerable situation, I think, having him chase around KAT on out on the open court.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green analyzes the strategic complexities of the Joel Embiid vs. Karl-Anthony Towns matchup, suggesting Embiid might be better off guarding someone else to preserve his health and avoid being pulled away from the rim.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Who's going to be the swing players for both of these teams in this series? OG Anunoby is going to have to swing this series. Dark horse for swing player in this series, Jordan Clarkson coming off the bench. I think will be huge in this series. They're going to need Jordan Clarkson off the bench. With his scoring ability, they're going to need some of that because I think at times, Nick Nurse is going to throw some funky things at KAT, some funky things at Jalen Brunson, and you're going to need a spark like Jordan Clarkson to come in and change some of these games. So I think when I look at that side, swing player. When I look at the 76ers, how well can Kelly Oubre Jr. play? Can he swing the series for the 76ers? Quentin Grimes off the bench, can he swing the series for the 76ers? I think ultimately, those are important. Andre Drummond off the bench, can he swing the series for the 76ers? Can he come in and neutralize Mitchell Robinson? Don't be surprised if you see some two-big lineups, right? You need to see some two-big lineups, put KAT at the four, put Mitchell Robinson at the five. How does a smaller 76ers team combat that? I think we need to see some of that. But ultimately, winning this series, the Knicks should win this series, and ultimately I will pick to win this series, but the 76ers are more than capable. I don't think they'll have enough ultimately to beat the Knicks, so I'm going to take the Knicks in this series, and I'm going to take the Knicks in six.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green identifies key swing players for both the Knicks (OG Anunoby, Jordan Clarkson) and the 76ers (Kelly Oubre Jr., Quentin Grimes, Andre Drummond), highlighting their potential to impact the series' outcome through scoring, defense, or strategic matchups.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Speaking of Austin Rivers, you know, I saw he said he's bewildered and it's ridiculous of what I said. And I just find it interesting that a guy who was the 10th pick in my draft, I was 35, who's on his second act, I'm still on Act 1, would say such things. He goes, 'Draymond's never been a scorer.' Well, Austin, you and I averaged the same amount of points in high school when you were a scorer. You know, so I don't know what would qualify Austin Rivers to speak about scoring when in high school, me and you averaged the same amount of points. I say high school because that's when you were at your best. That's when Austin Rivers was Austin Rivers in high school. And so that's why I point out the high school scoring because I want to make it fair. I want to speak about him when he was at his best. And he was at his best at Winter Park, if I remember correctly. He had ESPN games, like that's when he was at his best. When he was faster than everybody and can just put his head down and drive right and get to the rim. And then in college, you know, he was still good. He was very featured at Duke and, you know, had a very big moment, you know, where he hit the the three on the wing, like, you got to give him credit. That's when he was at his best. You know, well, in college, he averaged almost 17 points a game in the Big Ten. Very limited possessions. You know, so I I only want to speak about, you know, Austin at his best. Because NBA careers, like, should he really talk about my NBA career? I don't know that that's the case. I'm still with my first team. He was gone from his first team in two years.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green directly challenges Austin Rivers's criticism of his scoring, highlighting their comparable high school scoring averages and Rivers's shorter tenure with his first NBA team, questioning Rivers's authority to comment on his career.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Austin Rivers received the biggest bailout in US history prior to President Trump, bailout the airlines when they needed it. Austin Rivers received the biggest bailout in US history. Excuse me, in world history, in US history, received the biggest bailout in US history when his dad gave him $42 million. And I tip my hat to Doc. I pray that one day, you know, I mean, it won't be $42 million then because NBA's going up so much. But I pray that I can give DJ $200 million or give Deuce $250 million. I pray that I can do that one day. So I tip my hat to Doc and his incredible bailout of his son and putting good money in his pocket, man. Like I I really tip my cap to him. But, you know, if you, you know, if you listen to the whole thing, the whole three minutes of what I spoke about. What you what you what a competent basketball mind would have heard was, 'Man, this guy who wanted to do this, who thought he was this, changed his game and then still became this because that's what worked best for the team.' Never shared those gripes because they didn't matter. And by the way, still don't matter.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green controversially claims Austin Rivers received the 'biggest bailout in US history' when his father, Doc Rivers, signed him to a $42 million contract, implying nepotism and questioning Rivers's career legitimacy.
